protocol: train+val+test all from Celeb-DF v2; splits disjoint by CELEBRITY IDENTITY
comparability_warning: NOT comparable to EXP-001 (0.7076) or EXP-005 (0.6564), which held out an entire unseen dataset. Unseen-identity is an easier task.
tooling_note: eval_face_crops.py prints a hardcoded '=== CROSS-DATASET ===' header inherited from EXP-005. It is incorrect for this run.

splits.youtube_real_fallback: each id-less clip (e.g. 00109.mp4) treated as its own identity

extraction.accounting: 8395 = 6445 kept (4607+747+1091) + 1950 dropped (325 spanning videos x 6 frames)

identity_key_decomposition.note: '56 test identities' overstates diversity: 42 are single YouTube-real clips
identity_key_decomposition.fakes_come_only_from: the 14 celebrity identities; id11 and id12 contribute 0 fakes, so 12 effective

at_tuned.finding: target 0.05 -> actual 0.1048 on test; ~2x. Val-tuned thresholds do not transfer even across identities.

test_composition_derived.method: counted directly from test_celeb-df-v2_heldout_identity.csv (previously back-solved from metrics; the two agree exactly)
test_composition_derived.why: the identity split dropped 325 spanning videos, mostly synthesis clips (two identities each), inverting Celeb-DF's usual fake-heavy balance

uncertainty.note: crops from one video are correlated; effective n is the VIDEO count, not the crop count
uncertainty.defensible_claim: ROC-AUC in the low-to-mid 0.9s; the second decimal is not resolved
uncertainty.binding_constraint: 26 fake test videos from 12-14 celebrity identities

finding: POSITIVE. The face branch detects manipulations of unseen identities at ROC-AUC 0.9644 (+/-0.05) with 91% recall at 7.3% FPR. Combined with EXP-001/005 (0.66-0.71 cross-dataset), this locates the branch's weakness specifically in DATASET/DOMAIN shift rather than an inability to learn manipulation artifacts.
limitations: 26 fake test videos from 12-14 identities -> wide intervals (binding limitation)
Celeb-DF v2 repurposed from its spreadsheet 'External Test' role; spent for this checkpoint
val-tuned threshold did not transfer (0.05 target -> 0.1048 actual)

second_dataset_blocked.dfdc: kaggle:pranay22077/dfdc-10 - 96.5GB vs ~75GB Colab disk; loose mp4s with no per-part archives; Kaggle rate-limits per-file downloads at ~80 (observed twice)
second_dataset_blocked.ffpp: kaggle:ahmedelbanby/faceforensicsplusplus-c23-deepfakebench-structure - PNG frames not mp4, AND contains Celeb-DF under frames/Celeb-DF/ (silent leakage against this test set)

deviation_from_spreadsheet.reason: no second dataset obtainable (see second_dataset_blocked); this is why the result is identity-disjoint, not cross-dataset
deviation_from_spreadsheet.consequence: Celeb-DF v2 is spent as a held-out set for this checkpoint. Once FF++ is available, restore it to its held-out role and do NOT evaluate this checkpoint on it as if unseen.
